take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only for different access, dialect or stance. If one prompt can do it, write that prompt.
Failures happen at handoffs between agents, so check the seams. Nothing in the setup verifies that the final briefing is true.
Giving an agent a permission is a separate decision from letting it write files. The demo's approve-before-send pattern is how I would do it.

monday.move: Pick one recurring analysis job where the wiki and document folders are already in use, and run the one-agent version before I try anything multi-agent. Then judge whether the output beats what a person on my team produces.
monday.who: Me, plus one analyst I trust to tell me honestly if it is rubbish
monday.when: Probably later in the week, if the steering group calendar allows
monday.stop_condition: Stop if I cannot verify its claims against the sources within an hour, or if it needs data the GDPR people have not cleared.
monday.blocker: Calendar, and no way yet to check whether the synthesis is correct.

misconception.why: Wait-and-see is still my instinct. But the demo and the retrievers exercise showed something that was not possible two years ago, and the course said plainly that splitting is often unnecessary and that correctness is unverified. That is not how the last programmes were sold. I do not think it blows over, but I am not convinced it changes my business yet.

one_line: Less hype than I expected. It told me up front that one agent is usually enough and that nobody checks the briefing is true. I am still waiting to see it hold up on a real problem.
